lead: Rankings, growth narratives and policy arguments all depend on what the source actually measures. Today’s opening coverage separates conditional forecasts, reported approvals and paper values from completed outcomes.

sections.title: What a forecast or ranking actually establishes
sections.intro: A sparse ranking interface and a conditional superintelligence essay require different checks.

sections.title: Reporting to authorities needs context
sections.intro: A secondhand account, an inaccessible court report and a leadership excerpt do not establish universal legal rules.

sections.title: Usage growth has a cost side
sections.intro: Agent-created issues, trial abuse and missing demand arguments measure different parts of product economics.

sections.title: Approvals, hiring and demonstrations are different stages
sections.intro: Chip licensing, a reported development role and a console interface do not prove deployment outcomes.

sections.title: Paper gains and negotiating prices remain conditional
sections.intro: Estimated stakes and acquisition talks are not cash distributions or completed deals.

sections.title: Market reactions do not isolate causes
sections.intro: A trading roundup, regional sell-off and postponed offering describe different stages and evidentiary limits.

sections.title: Industrial monitoring meets access constraints
sections.intro: Equipment analytics and reported remote-compute licensing scrutiny require distinct technical and legal checks.

sections.title: Listings and interface rollouts have narrow meanings
sections.intro: Job advertisements are not employment totals, and a desktop rollout statement is not account-specific availability.

sections.title: Time windows matter in trading excerpts
sections.intro: A homepage link and inconsistent headline and excerpt prevent a precise price or offering-total comparison.

sections.title: Proof claims meet independent review
sections.intro: An author statement, a formalization report and a separate ETH review announcement are different stages of mathematical scrutiny.

sections.title: Hardware gains need the right denominator
sections.intro: Pre-silicon CPU comparisons and optical-operation energy do not automatically translate into whole-system wins.

sections.title: Nearly correct is not complete
sections.intro: Integration scoring, agent coordination and deferred schemas expose distinct limits behind automation headlines.

sections.title: Isolation must be tested at several layers
sections.intro: Synthetic websites, shared inference state and incomplete screenshot controls address different security boundaries.

sections.title: Extraction and computer use change product boundaries
sections.intro: Specialized models and background app control come with rollout and evaluation limits.

sections.title: Financing totals are not trading outcomes
sections.intro: Overallotment exercise, private valuations and intraday share moves must remain separate.

sections.title: Feed inclusion is not a substantive AI claim
sections.intro: A cultural review and an inaccessible podcast discussion have different limits from technical reporting.
